title: ICC Registry advises judges: Duterte's unexplained exits could fuel disinformation
summary: As the trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte nears, the International Criminal Court (ICC) Registry is asking Trial Chamber III to consider explaining its authorizations before allowing him to…
byline: Jay-vee Marasigan Pangan, Andy Peñafuerte III

blocks.text: As the trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte nears, the International Criminal Court (ICC) Registry is asking Trial Chamber III to consider explaining its authorizations before allowing him to leave the courtroom.
In its observations published on October 7, the Registry said victims and affected communities have shown “strong interest” in following Duterte’s trial live, particularly from the Philippines.

For people watching the trial online, the Registry said the concern could be even greater if Duterte suddenly disappears from the courtroom feed without explanation as it could fuel speculation and disinformation.

“This would create fertile ground for disinformation and speculations [sic], e.g., about his health, which is a recurring topic of interest in the Philippines, or the effect that his leaving and entering the courtroom could have on a witness.”
To avoid this, the Registry proposed that any standing permission for Duterte to leave the courtroom be publicly explained on the first day of trial.
It said judges should give “as much concrete details as possible” about the arrangement and could repeat a brief explanation at the start of each trial day.
The Registry also said witnesses should be informed in advance if such an arrangement is in place.
The Registry also expects that Philippine media would follow the proceedings “very intensively”, including “smallest details”.
“Journalists are certain to pay attention to the smallest details related to Mr Duterte’s appearance and conduct,” it said.
The Registry also said victims and affected communities place “paramount importance” on Duterte’s presence during the proceedings.

If Duterte does not attend in person, another option is a video link from the ICC Detention Center, subject to the Chamber’s approval. The Registry said he would still be able to communicate privately with his lawyers under that setup.
In a decision, Trial Chamber III has found Duterte fit for trial, stating he “he “is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings.”
It has also instructed the ICC Registry to “make necessary arrangements”, including a sitting schedule.
The fourth status conference is scheduled for October 13. The final one before the trial proceedings is set for November 2. — BAP, GMA News
